The African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank), in partnership with the Cross River State Government, the Nigeria Governors’ Forum (NGF) and the Forum of State Investment Promotion Agencies in Nigeria (FoSIPAN), will convene the sixth African Sub-Sovereign Governments Network (AfSNET) Investment Conference in Calabar, Cross River State, from November 12 to 14, 2026. The conference will bring together African subnational governments, investors, financial institutions and development partners to strengthen project preparation, attract investment and expand trade opportunities across the continent. Established by Afreximbank in 2021, AfSNET provides a platform for African states, provinces, counties, municipalities and other subnational authorities to showcase investment opportunities, engage financiers and strengthen their capacity to develop projects capable of attracting funding. Since its inception, the network has convened more than 1,400 delegates across five editions, with participation from 21 African countries, and facilitated more than $3.2 billion in investment opportunities and transactions. The sixth edition will place greater emphasis on converting investment potential into bankable projects and transactions, reflecting the importance of effective project preparation and direct engagement between governments and sources of capital. The three-day conference, scheduled to hold at the Calabar International Convention Centre, will feature investment promotion training, project preparation workshops, investment showcases, business-to-government deal rooms and investment pitch sessions designed to connect subnational governments with investors and financiers. Discussions will also cover special economic zones, tourism, the creative economy, trade-enabling infrastructure and regional economic integration. Afreximbank considers subnational governments critical to Africa’s economic transformation because they are responsible for many of the local infrastructure, production and investment activities needed to strengthen regional trade and industrial capacity. Through AfSNET, the bank seeks to help these authorities improve investment promotion, prepare viable projects and access capital to support the implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). The initiative is intended to translate continental trade ambitions into productive investment and economic activity within African states and regions, particularly by strengthening local businesses, infrastructure and productive sectors. Examples of projects associated with the network include the $40 million Med Aditus Pharmaceuticals project in Kisumu, Kenya, which is under preparation and envisages a manufacturing plant capable of producing at least two billion tablets and capsules annually for the treatment of non-communicable diseases. In Nigeria, the Cross River State Government has appointed Afreximbank as financial adviser for the development of the $1.7 billion Bakassi Deep Seaport project. The proposed port has the potential to strengthen maritime trade connectivity and support industrial and logistics development. Another example is the $871 million Nyanza Light Metals project in South Africa, which is under development and involves a titanium dioxide pigment manufacturing plant with a planned annual production capacity of 80,000 metric tonnes. The project is expected to support mineral beneficiation and industrialisation. These projects illustrate the range of investment opportunities that can support manufacturing, infrastructure development and regional value chains, although their respective development stages differ. Speaking ahead of the conference, Bassey Otu, governor of Cross River State, said hosting the event would provide the state with an opportunity to engage African and international investors, showcase its investment opportunities and build partnerships to support sustainable economic development. He said the state looked forward to welcoming governments, businesses, financiers and development partners to Calabar, while demonstrating the role subnational governments could play in driving trade and investment under the AfCFTA. Kanayo Awani, executive vice president, Intra-African Trade and Export Development at Afreximbank, said subnational governments were central to Africa’s economic transformation because much of the continent’s production, infrastructure development and investment took place at that level. “Through AfSNET, we are creating a practical platform through which states, provinces and counties can strengthen project preparation, connect viable opportunities with capital and build the productive capacity needed to expand intra-African trade,” Awani said. She added that the conference would focus on bankable projects, investment mobilisation and partnerships capable of supporting industrialisation, value addition and stronger regional value chains. For Afreximbank, strengthening the ability of subnational governments to prepare projects and engage investors is an important part of expanding access to capital for economic development. The Calabar conference will therefore seek to build practical links between investment opportunities and financing, while equipping participating authorities with the knowledge, networks and tools needed to develop projects capable of attracting long-term investment. She closely tracks market movements, monetary policy decisions, company disclosures, regulatory actions, economic indicators, and global developments, and interprets what they mean for businesses, investors, policymakers, and households. Her reporting helps readers understand complex issues such as inflation trends, foreign exchange market dynamics, interest rate decisions, bank performance, and investment risks. She also covers major international events and periodically travels to Washington, D.C., to report on the World Bank/IMF Spring and Annual Meetings. Her dedication to financial journalism has earned her multiple recognitions and invitations to high-level professional development programmes. She is an alumna of the International Visitors Leadership Programme (IVLP) in the United States and holds an Advanced Financial Journalism Certificate from the Press Association Training in London, UK. Her other notable achievements include completing the Lagos Business School CMC Programme, the Bloomberg Media Africa Initiative Programme, and a Master Class in Journalism at Rhodes University in South Africa.
